sections.html:
Carter County covers about 412 square miles of northeastern Kentucky. Grayson is the seat, Olive Hill is the only other city, and Interstate 64 and US 60 carry traffic through. The 2020 census counted 26,627 people, and the 2025 estimate is 26,149.

Most homes sit outside town limits and many are decades old. Of the 10,664 households, 75.7 percent owned their home, and 12.6 percent of the 12,206 housing units were empty. Only about one resident in five lived in an area the census treats as urban. For a seller, that means a lot of rural parcels, farm tracts and older frame houses, where acreage, wells, septic and road access can matter as much as the building.

sections.h2: Who bills and collects the tax
sections.html:
Three courthouse offices split the job. The Property Valuation Administrator values each parcel, the county clerk prints bills and inherits the unpaid ones, and the sheriff takes payment through autumn and winter. All three are at 300 West Main Street in Grayson, so a single trip can settle most questions.

Calling the wrong desk wastes a morning. Questions about worth belong with the PVA, questions about this year's bill with the sheriff, and anything already late with the clerk.

Carter County offices that handle property tax
OfficeAddressPhoneHours
Property Valuation Administration300 West Main Street, Suite 214, Grayson(606) 474-5663Mon to Fri 8:30 am to 4:00 pm; last Saturday of the month 8:30 am to noon
Sheriff (tax collection)300 West Main Street, Grayson(606) 474-5616Mon to Fri 8:30 am to 4:00 pm; last Saturday of the month 8:30 am to noon
County Clerk (tax bills, delinquent taxes)300 West Main Street, Grayson(606) 474-5188Mon to Fri 8:30 am to 4:00 pm; Grayson office open the last Saturday of each month, Olive Hill office open Saturdays 8:00 am to noon

The clerk also runs an Olive Hill location with its own Saturday hours.

Under KRS 134.015 the calendar is the same every year. A bill appears around the first of October, and what you owe shifts with the date of payment.

  • Up to November 1, full payment earns a 2 percent reduction.
  • From November 2 through year end, you pay the amount on the bill.
  • Any day in January adds 5 percent.
  • Once February starts, the penalty is 10 percent and the sheriff's add-on fee kicks in.

Tax is your personal debt from the assessment date, and a lien on the land lasts eleven years regardless of who buys the house. If a bill never turns up, call the sheriff at (606) 474-5616 and ask how mailed and in-person payments are handled.

Your first call is to the PVA, since a conference there opens the door to every later step. The roll is open for public viewing for thirteen days starting the first Monday of May, and your conference must take place inside that period.

When the PVA won't budge, hand the clerk a written petition no later than the workday after viewing ends. Identify the parcel and give your opinion of its open-market price. A local board hears the case about a month later and wants proof: sale listings, construction costs, insurance policies. Petitions with no evidence get denied. Owners who skip the board lose the right to go on to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals.

Filing doesn't pause the bill. You keep paying on the figure you claimed until the case ends, and a higher final value triggers a supplemental bill.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid bills after April 15
sections.html:
Every bill still open on April 15 moves from the sheriff to the county clerk and becomes a certificate of delinquency. The clerk reports that totals jump by about 40 percent once the added charges are counted. Personal checks are refused on these bills. Cash, money orders, company checks and cards (with a user fee) are accepted.

The clerk will sometimes set up a payment plan: a third of the balance up front and the rest within 90 days. Miss that deadline and the bill goes back on the delinquent list, with the money already paid kept and credited, not refunded.

  • The clerk advertises about 30 days before the sale and posts the list online.
  • The sale is held in late summer, in the fiscal courtroom at 10 am.
  • Bidders register at least ten days ahead, and the lien assignment fee is $46.

Whoever wins a certificate gains the right to collect from you. Paying before April 15 is far cheaper.

The break goes to owners who live in the house and are at retirement age or totally disabled. A fixed sum comes off the assessed value before the rate is applied. That sum stands at $49,100 for assessment years 2025 and 2026, with a new figure every second year.

Apply at the Carter County PVA, which also knows the current figure. A birth certificate, driver's license or passport proves age. Disability applicants renew every year, with exceptions for owners with a service-connected rating and owners found permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: Selling a Carter County house that still owes tax
sections.html:
Yes. The balance is paid out of the sale price by the title company. First get this year's payoff from the sheriff. Then check with the clerk for any earlier year filed as delinquent, because a recorded certificate appears in a title search and must be paid or released to give the buyer a clean title.

Timing changes the cost. A bill still with the sheriff carries only the 5 or 10 percent penalty, while one at the clerk adds fees and interest. When the house is inherited, vacant or needs work, a cash purchaser who takes it as it stands can settle the tax from your proceeds, so you needn't bring money to closing.

Written balances from both offices should go to the closing agent before you sign a contract. Ask that the payoff and any release be shown as separate lines.

A little preparation shortens the process. Gather your parcel number or street address, your most recent bill and your deed. If you plan to claim the homestead exemption, bring a photo ID, and for a disability claim bring the paperwork from the agency or retirement system that classified you.

Visit before the last Saturday of the month if you need a weekend slot: the PVA, sheriff and clerk open that morning until noon, and the Olive Hill clerk office keeps its own Saturday hours. Weekday hours at the courthouse end at 4:00 pm, so don't leave a payoff request to the last hour of the day when a closing is close.

If a cash sale is on your list, a buyer who purchases as-is skips repairs and showings. You still need the payoff letters, so request them early.

faqs.q: Which office takes Carter County property tax payments?
faqs.a: The sheriff, at 300 West Main Street in Grayson, phone (606) 474-5616. Bills unpaid past April 15 are handled by the county clerk.

faqs.q: What if my Carter County tax bill never arrives?
faqs.a: Call the sheriff's office with your name or parcel number. Ask how it takes payments by mail, and confirm the address before you send a check.

faqs.q: How late can I file a Carter County assessment appeal?
faqs.a: The petition goes to the clerk by the next workday after the May inspection window closes. A conference with the PVA must come first.

faqs.q: Will the Carter County clerk accept my personal check on a delinquent bill?
faqs.a: No. Personal checks are refused on delinquent bills. Cash, money orders, company checks and cards are accepted, and cards carry a user fee.

faqs.q: Can I list my Carter County house while back taxes are open?
faqs.a: Yes. The payoff is taken from your proceeds at closing, so get written balances from the sheriff and the clerk before you sign a contract.
